title: India's 13-Storey Stepwell With 3,500 Steps
description: Chand Baori in Abhaneri, Rajasthan, built over a thousand years ago.

scenes.narration: Three and a half thousand steps, in perfect zigzags, going down thirteen storeys.
scenes.image_prompt: Chand Baori stepwell with thousands of zigzag steps descending to green water, symmetry

scenes.narration: This is Chand Baori, in Abhaneri village, Rajasthan, built around the 9th century.
scenes.image_prompt: Rajasthani village with a giant square stepwell, desert landscape, 9th century

scenes.narration: In the dry desert, water is life. This well stores rainwater through the year.
scenes.image_prompt: monsoon rain pouring into a deep stepwell, dark clouds

scenes.narration: It's about thirty metres deep, and much cooler at the bottom than at the surface.
scenes.image_prompt: view from the bottom of a deep stepwell looking up at layered steps and sky

scenes.narration: Villagers gather here to rest, talk and escape the heat.
scenes.image_prompt: Rajasthani villagers in colourful turbans and saris resting on stepwell steps

scenes.narration: A temple to Harshat Mata, goddess of joy, stands right beside it.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient carved stone temple ruins beside a stepwell, warm light

scenes.narration: Filmmakers love it. It's appeared in Hollywood movies.
scenes.image_prompt: dramatic cinematic shot of a geometric stepwell at golden hour

scenes.narration: It's over a thousand years old. Would you walk all the way down? Comment below.
scenes.image_prompt: Chand Baori stepwell at sunset with long shadows
